nodes.title: How much prefill fits in this iteration
nodes.behavior: The adder continues the unfinished request, then scans waiting requests. Compute budgets charge extend plus replay rows. budget_state checks memory first, input exhaustion second, then chunk exhaustion, so input events can mask a simultaneously exhausted chunk budget. In the normal chunked path, shape selection fits chunk/KV limits; max_prefill_tokens stops subsequent admission and is not a universal hard bound on an individual chunk.
conditions: AGG or PD prefill; normal PrefillAdder path.
confounders: DP divides declared chunk size; mixed decode consumes budget; page alignment; replay rows; max request limits; one unchunked request can exceed nominal input cap.

Equal input and chunk limits receive equal compute charges; the emitted input-budget event does not identify which cap alone should change. Raising only the input cap can merely expose the chunk-budget event without increasing admitted work.

MegaMoE startup validates aligned effective per-rank chunk size against SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK; that environment cap also sizes symmetric buffers. Increasing chunk size can require a coupled workspace change with additional memory demand.
nodes.hypothesis: If token budget binds with queued work and spare KV, a larger batch may improve P capacity; it may increase TTFT/ITL and workspace demand.
nodes.next_test: First compare resolved input/chunk limits and admitted residuals. Test a coherent effective chunk/workspace budget only if full-run evidence supports more prefill work; document coupled prerequisites as one budget intervention, retain sufficient physical memory, and compare useful prefill service with decode/latency cost. An event-name change alone is not improvement.
nodes.remaining_gap: Not all specialized DLLM/ignore-EOS stops have reason logs; inspect residual budget/queue evidence.
nodes.evidence: code-audited; causal performance effect requires paired experiment

nodes.title: Request rows and request-count limits
nodes.behavior: get_num_allocatable_reqs takes the minimum of PP microbatch budget and nonnegative free request rows plus already-held rows minus pending beam-member rows, with a further beam-width quotient when applicable. Continued requests can retain rows. The request_slots event is emitted at both the pre-sort no-room gate and a candidate-loop limit; token capacity is a separate constraint.
conditions: Interpret separately for P, AGG and D; D has dedicated preallocation.
confounders: Per-rank effective limits; held rows; in-transfer rows; PP microbatches; LoRA eligibility; graph capture size.
A deliberately bounded admission cap can protect decode graph coverage. Its gate firing does not by itself mean the cap should rise; raising it can reintroduce a slower execution regime.
nodes.hypothesis: If row/count gates bind before memory, more rows may raise occupancy; it can also increase graph/workspace memory and decode latency.
nodes.next_test: Compare resolved row/PP limits, held/beam reservations, graph coverage and full-run service. Preserve a graph-protecting cap until a complete comparison shows its admission cost outweighs its benefit; widening capture requires separate memory validation.
nodes.remaining_gap: The aggregate request_slots event has no site or component-budget fields. A future sampled receipt should retain the already-computed PP/free/held/beam budgets and candidate threshold at the actual stop, without extra pool/readiness calls. Counts are gate encounters, not requests or blocked time.
nodes.evidence: R11 first five90s windows retain11request-slot encounters on ranks1/2 while sampled running maxima remain<=62 against resolved64. Ten-second gauges can miss transient work; competing PP/held-row terms also prevent attributing each event uniquely to max_running_requests. Full replay remains pending.

conditions: HiCache/storage enabled and relevant metric producer instantiated.
confounders: Host Engram footprint; NUMA/huge pages; device victims; returning-turn locality; storage backend; write policy.

Active KV usage excludes evictable cache. Device eviction can preserve data in L2. L2 host eviction is distinct from device tokens dropped without backup. Cache TP labels use attention coordinates under DP attention.
DeepSeekV4 host-used/total gauges describe logical FULL anchors; the anchor itself owns no KV tensor. Physical compressed/SWA pools and process/cgroup memory need separate accounting.

nodes.title: Explicit decode interval defers prefill before budget checks
nodes.behavior: After an extend batch, the configured interval is armed. Each subsequent scheduling encounter decrements it and skips prefill admission while it remains active. Under attention DP the extend flag is synchronized across ranks.
conditions: Normal scheduler path; DLLM branch bypasses this gate. Event requires tuning_observation_interval > 0.
confounders: A deferral can occur without waiting work; continuing chunks are separate from waiting_queue. Other ranks can arm the shared cadence. Gate encounters are not completed decode forwards or elapsed wait. Downstream capacity checks are not reached in deferred passes.

A fixed step-count interval is not a fixed wall-clock prefill frequency. Slower eager decode can reduce prefill opportunities per second without any cadence config change; diagnose graph coverage before attributing the slower prefill rate to token budgets or choosing a new interval.
nodes.hypothesis: With queued or continuing prefill work, a long decode interval can reduce prefill service even with free KV and no token-budget encounter. Reducing it may increase logical throughput while worsening decode ITL.
nodes.next_test: At fixed concurrency, topology, cache warmup and budgets, compare interval24 versus a lower value only after sustained queued-work deferrals are observed. Compare prefill service, total/output throughput, TTFT and p10 decode speed; reverse the change if the workload tradeoff is unfavorable.
nodes.remaining_gap: No exposed wall-time or oldest eligible request age is attributed to this gate. Queue presence does not prove all queued requests are otherwise eligible.
nodes.evidence: CPU behavior and four-rank GPU gate emissions verified. GB200 C256 paired900-second diagnostic24→12: lower TTFT/queues, slower decode and−5.37%totalTPS/GPU. These are preliminary prefix observations with closed-loop/cache confounders; a full-hour original-config baseline is next, before selecting another intervention.

nodes.title: Which waiting request gets prefill work next
nodes.behavior: Shortest-prefill-first sorts by temporary duplicate-prefix deferral, estimated uncached tokens, then queue-entry time. Age breaks work-size ties rather than overriding larger work. Its chunk limit reserves capacity for shorter waiting requests, reducing a continuing long request to at least one page when reservation fills the budget. HRRN instead uses processed-token aging divided by estimated uncached work; policies change both ordering and prefix locality. Switching to HRRN also removes shortest_prefill_chunk_limit reservation for shorter waiting requests; it is a policy-package intervention, not an ordering-only change. Remaining compute/KV/chunk constraints still apply. HRRN age is accumulated processed prefill tokens since queue entry, not wall-clock seconds; fully cached work and temporary duplicate-prefix deferral retain their own priority. In the unified path, queue entry/reentry snapshots the token counter; run_batch advances it by extend_num_tokens before model execution. It is submitted prefill work, not completed GPU work. HRRN cost is max(0, origin_input_length - matched_prefix), while SPF cost is max(1, origin_input_length + output_length - matched_prefix). HRRN exact ties use request-ID lexical order internally; do not expose IDs in telemetry.
conditions: Cache-aware policy with prefix matching enabled; inspect resolved policy and specialized paths.
The existing shortest-prefill diagnostic log is sampled once per128 sorting calls; it is not a heartbeat or oldest-request receipt.

prefill.chunk_slot is emitted only in the shortest-prefill-first path when another unfinished chunk exists and a new request would need chunking. Its absence after a policy switch is a producer-population change, not proof of spare chunk capacity.
Sorting occurs before candidate budget/LoRA/prefetch/staging admission checks. A sorted head or non-deferred prefix candidate is not established eligible work.

Configured HRRN (and LPM) switches to FCFS above128waiting requests in _determine_active_policy; SPF does not. Read effective_policy per sampled pass. R7 incidence/impact is not established by source behavior alone.
confounders: Estimated uncached work differs from total input length and from actual transfer/replay cost.
Cadence, compute budgets, capacity and cache readiness can delay even the first-ranked request.
First-forward queue histograms observe only admitted requests; clearing old backlog can increase measured tail counts and mean queue time.
Client/router/tokenizer delay and later chunk service contribute to TTFT beyond the initial scheduler queue wait.

A policy switch changes continuation reservation and which chunk-slot checks can emit, even with identical configured chunk/input budgets. Compare actual admitted work and completed outcomes rather than treating disappearing event names as a gain.

Unified reentry resets both queue-entry time and arrival token counter; current-episode age is not cumulative lifetime starvation. Output-bearing/retracted work can have different HRRN/SPF cost estimates, but incidence must be observed before assigning performance impact.
nodes.hypothesis: Under sustained mixed-work queues, ordering can favor repeated cheap admissions while expensive requests wait, hurting trajectory progress and tails. A different policy may improve fairness but reduce cache locality or useful throughput.

Preserving FULL host pages by compensating the ratio need not preserve SWA/sidecar geometry, physical host bytes, device retention or hit distribution.

conditions: SWA cap mode requires an explicit request cap and sliding-window size, no operator SWA ratio, non-unified pools, and positive chunked prefill unless decode-only. Other modes have different sizing rules.

confounders: An explicit swa_prefix_tails fixes prefix-tail count, not the request-dependent SWA floor. With no explicit tails, the default can depend on the row cap too.
